cards.title: cartesianMesh — a robust hex mesh when snap is unstable
cards.when: complex geometry, snappy gives poor snap/layers, a predictable hex mesh is needed
cards.statement: cartesianMesh (cfMesh inside OpenFOAM v2512) builds an octree hex mesh from surfaceFile with an explicit renameBoundary; it is more robust than snap on complex surfaces, but has no near-wall layers and leaves a staircase at the boundary.
recipe: renameBoundary.newPatchNames for inlet/outlet/walls/interface — otherwise everything becomes unmatched/wall
np>1: decomposePar -force → mpirun -np N cartesianMesh -parallel → reconstructParMesh -constant -mergeTol 1e-6 → rm -rf processor*
take the binary from the OpenFOAM installation (platforms/*/bin), not from env/cfmesh-1.2.0
evidence: OpenFOAM v2512 ships cartesianMesh in platforms/linux64GccDPInt32Opt/bin

cards.title: pMesh — Voronoi polyhedra: more cells, better volume, worse non-orthogonality
cards.when: a polyhedral mesh or an accurate domain volume is needed
cards.statement: At the same sizes pMesh gives 3.7–4.0× more cells and non-ortho stays around 61° (the project gate fails on 12–14 faces), but the volume converges more accurately than hex (−0.003…−0.12 % versus −0.05…−5.0 %). It does not run in parallel (argList::noParallel()).
recipe: subdict meshQualitySettings { maxNonOrthogonality 60; maxSkewness 2.0; ... } — in 1.2.0 it removes faces > 60° without changing the cell count (2 of 4 cases start passing the gate)
for CHT the interface is mismatched again (126 464 ↔ 125 622 faces) — do not use it as a conformal interface
evidence: exp-008: 3.7–4.0× cells, ~61°, more accurate volume; meshQualitySettings helps in 2 of 4 cases

cards.title: Layers on top of tetra break conformity — do not do it
cards.when: tempted to add near-wall layers to a gmsh tetra mesh via cfMesh
cards.statement: cfMesh layers on top of tetra break conformity and quality (interface 2612 → 3272 faces, non-ortho 86.9–88.9°), and gmsh 4.15.2 does not build 3D layers: the BoundaryLayer field has no SurfacesList, so the volume silently gets 0 prisms (D-018). The verified path for CHT is HXT (gmsh Algorithm3D=10) without layers, or snappy castellatedBufferLayer (exp-005), not cfMesh on top of tetra.
recipe: gmsh.OCC: Mesh.Algorithm3D = 10 (HXT) — the best result in exp-015
layers: BoundaryLayer field (NbLayers, Ratio, hwall_n, hfar, Quads, SurfacesList)
after gmshToFoam: checkMesh; if non-ortho > 60°, reduce the first layers instead of adding cfMesh layers
evidence: exp-015: gmsh 4.15.2 without 3D layers; cfMesh layers on top of tetra degraded the quality; HXT Algorithm3D=10 best

cards.title: Route D: conformal CHT from OCC geometry via gmsh
cards.when: a conformal interface between two regions (fluid+solid) is needed without snappy
cards.statement: OCC path: domain box + import of the solid STEP → occ.fragment → two volume groups, fluid and solid → the outer surfaces are assigned to physical groups sym_*, the interface stays WITHOUT a group (then gmshToFoam makes it internal) → .msh MSH2 → gmshToFoam → splitMeshRegions.
recipe: interface: surfaces adjacent to TWO volumes — without a physical group
Mesh.MshFileVersion 2.2; MeshSizeMin = size*0.25; multiply the coordinates by --scale 0.001 before write
set the patch types after splitMeshRegions by editing constant/<region>/polyMesh/boundary (changeDictionary does not work)
evidence: exp-016 scripts/build_pore_sym.py — verified: h=0.3 mm, 6 flat symmetryPlane patches, Mesh OK
